subject: Animation
title: The Multiplane Camera: Depth in 2D
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Multiplane Camera: Depth in 2D.

hook.text: Disney invented the multiplane camera in 1937 to give flat 2D animation the illusion of depth.

buildup.text: The camera filmed through layers of glass, each holding different elements at different distances.

discovery.text: Moving the layers at different speeds created parallax — foreground moved fast, background moved slowly.

twist.text: The multiplane camera cost $70,000 to build in 1937 — equivalent to over $1.4 million today.

climax.text: The multiplane camera gave Snow White a visual depth that no other animated film had achieved before.

punchline.text: Layers of glass gave flat drawings the illusion of a deep world.

quiz.question: How did the multiplane camera create depth in 2D animation?
options: It used 3D glasses for the audience
It filmed through layers of glass at different distances, moving them at different speeds for parallax
It projected images onto curved screens

details.summary: Disney's multiplane camera stacked multiple painted glass layers at different distances from the camera. As the camera moved, closer layers shifted faster than distant ones, creating a convincing parallax depth effect in hand-drawn animation.
details.whyItMatters: The multiplane camera solved 2D animation's flatness problem. It added visual depth that made animated worlds feel three-dimensional and immersive, raising the cinematic quality of hand-drawn films.
takeaways: Multiple glass layers created parallax depth in 2D animation
Closer layers moved faster than distant layers during camera movement
The technique made hand-drawn animation feel three-dimensional

faq.question: When was the multiplane camera first used?
faq.answer: Disney's multiplane camera debuted in the 1937 short The Old Mill. It was then used extensively in Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs. The camera created groundbreaking depth effects that stunned audiences.

faq.question: Is the multiplane effect still used in modern animation?
faq.answer: The physical camera is obsolete, but the parallax principle is used universally. Digital compositing software easily creates multiplane effects, and 2D animation programs build the technique in as a standard feature.
